stem: A client receiving chemotherapy asks how to care for the mouth during treatment. Which instruction should the nurse include?

options.A: Brush the teeth and gums gently with a soft-bristle toothbrush and use a mild or bland mouth rinse as recommended.
options.B: Stop brushing the teeth during chemotherapy because routine oral hygiene increases the risk of mouth sores.
options.C: Use a stiff-bristle toothbrush to remove plaque more effectively when the oral tissues become tender.
options.D: Rely on mouth rinses alone after meals because mechanical cleaning of the teeth is unnecessary during treatment.

rationale: NCI guidance states that everyday oral care during chemotherapy includes keeping the mouth clean while being gentle with the oral tissues. Recommended measures include brushing the teeth and gums with a soft-bristle toothbrush and using mild or bland rinses. Regular oral hygiene may help prevent or decrease oral complications. Stopping oral hygiene, using a stiff brush, or substituting rinsing for needed mechanical cleaning can increase oral problems rather than prevent them.
educational_objective: Teach gentle, regular oral hygiene during chemotherapy, including soft-bristle toothbrushing and mild or bland rinses to support oral comfort and reduce treatment-related oral complications.
source_organization: National Cancer Institute (NCI), National Institutes of Health
source_document_title: Oral Complications of Cancer Therapies (PDQ®)–Patient Version
source_locator: Managing Oral Complications During and After Chemotherapy or Radiation Therapy — Regular Oral Care; Everyday oral care during chemotherapy and radiation therapy; Oral Mucositis — Cleaning the mouth
source_claim_supported: NCI states that regular oral hygiene may prevent or decrease complications during cancer treatment; everyday care includes gentle cleaning with a soft-bristle toothbrush, and mild or bland rinses are used to keep the mouth clean and soothe oral tissues.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort — activities of daily living/personal hygiene and comfort-related nursing care content
blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — oral hygiene and supportive comfort care
correction_summary: Rebuilt the original 'mucositis prevention' item into an evidence-supported oral-care teaching item. Replaced the generic ONS homepage with NCI PDQ and exact oral-care sections. Removed the implication that routine oral hygiene alone prevents chemotherapy-induced mucositis, removed protocol-dependent rinse wording, and remapped the item from Safety and Infection Prevention and Control to Basic Care and Comfort because the tested nursing action is personal oral hygiene/supportive care.
audit_findings: Original wording overstated general oral hygiene as a specific prevention strategy for chemotherapy-induced mucositis rather than supportive oral care that may reduce oral complications.
NCI directly supports soft-bristle toothbrushing and mild/bland rinses during chemotherapy and emphasizes gentle cleaning of oral tissues.
The final item avoids institution-specific rinse protocols and does not prescribe an unsupported universal mouthwash formulation.
Blueprint mapping was corrected to Basic Care and Comfort because the tested action is oral hygiene/supportive care rather than transmission-based infection control.
Independent adversarial review found no ambiguity, second valid answer, cueing, or unresolved source conflict.
